answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a refundable work bond. Every new agent starts hollow: no reputation, tiny transaction caps, and it must post a bond to enter. It earns a lantern mark only after peers verify real paid tasks on-chain, and the bond unlocks as verified work accumulates. To cross the ridge into full trading limits, an agent needs a long streak of verified work plus a larger bond. A sybil farmer must pay a fresh bond and do real work for each fake identity, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds and histories, more than any fake reputation is worth.
